match.reason: The only bank point is about government debt and budget deficits in Economics, which is a different idea from returns, bad debts and discounts in accounts receivable and payable.

draft.title: Returns, bad debts and discounts
card: Sales return
goods a customer sends back to the seller. The seller lowers the amount the customer owes, so accounts receivable falls.
Purchase return
goods the business sends back to a supplier. The business owes less, so accounts payable falls.
Bad debt
an amount a customer will not pay. The seller writes it off, which removes it from accounts receivable and records it as an expense.
Discount
a cut in the amount owed, offered to a customer who pays early. The customer pays less than the invoice total, and the seller receives less cash.
draft.remember: Returns and write-offs cut what is owed. A discount cuts what is paid for paying early.

a.q: Priya's Pantry sells goods on credit to a café. The café returns damaged goods. What happens in Priya's records?
opts: Accounts receivable falls
Accounts receivable rises
Accounts payable falls
Accounts payable rises
a.why: A sales return means the customer owes less, so the seller's accounts receivable falls. Accounts payable is what the business owes its own suppliers, and a customer's return does not change it.
a.clue: Priya is the seller, so think about what the café owes her.

b.q: Tom's Tyres buys stock on credit from a supplier and sends some faulty tyres back. Which result is correct?
opts: Tom owes the supplier less, so accounts payable falls
Tom is owed less by the supplier, so receivable falls
Tom writes the amount off as a bad debt
Tom receives a discount for paying the supplier early
b.why: Tom is the buyer, so a purchase return cuts what he owes and accounts payable falls. It is not a bad debt, because a bad debt is an amount a customer will not pay, and it is not a discount, because nothing was paid early.
b.clue: Tom is the buyer. Whose debt shrinks when goods go back?

b.best: Tom owes the supplier less, so accounts payable falls

problems.detail: The remember line says returns and write-offs cut what is owed, while a discount cuts what is paid. This implies a discount does not reduce the amount owed, but the card defines a discount as 'a cut in the amount owed'. A discount also reduces accounts receivable, so the remember line's neat split contradicts the card.

check.summary: Both questions are correct, each with one clear answer. The remember line splits returns and write-offs (cut what is owed) from discounts (cut what is paid), which contradicts the card's definition of a discount as a cut in the amount owed.
